goal: Build the floor. The big picture, number systems and signed numbers carry the vocabulary every later lesson assumes, so they go first while you are fresh. Answer every exam question inside each lesson before moving on.
drill: Convert between binary, hex and decimal until it is automatic; every later calculation leans on it. Then lunch, away from the desk.

goal: Every calculation topic in one run: floating point, image sizing, instruction formats, addressing and CPU performance. All formula work, each with a worked example to copy under pressure.
drill: The exam questions inside those lessons. Anything you miss, reread that block before moving on. Then eat, away from the desk, before the evening sitting.

goal: Start with fifteen minutes, book shut, recalling yesterday's conversions and formulas. Then pipelining and cache, which carry more marks than anything else and sit inside the compulsory Question One, and RISC against CISC for the objective half.
drill: Every pipeline and cache question inside those two lessons. They are Question One's heaviest parts.

window: Wednesday, 9:30 am to 12:30 pm, before the paper at 3
goal: Sit Question One of both papers against the clock, then the floating point, instruction format and pipeline questions you will choose for your other two. Finish on the one-page sheet, then eat and rest before the paper.
drill: In the hall: Question One is compulsory. For the other two, choose floating point, instruction formats with image sizing, and pipeline timing.

window: Only if you finish early: extra practice, not required
goal: Three practice papers in the real shape: Question One compulsory, then any two. Sit Question One of each against the clock, then the questions you would choose.
drill: Question One of each mock is worth more than a whole second paper.
